item.title: Israel says will take 'control' of security zone in south Lebanon
item.description: Israel said on Tuesday that its military would take control of south Lebanon up to the Litani River, around 30 kilometres (20 miles) from the border, as deadly strikes pounded the country.In the latest unprecedented step by Lebanese authorities since a new war erupted between Israel and Hezbollah, Lebanon's foreign ministry declared the Iranian ambassador persona non grata, giving him until Sunday to leave the country.

item.title: Modi, Trump discuss importance of keeping Strait of Hormuz open, U.S. envoy says
item.description: March 24 (Reuters) - Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. President Donald Trump spoke by phone on Tuesday and discussed the situation in the Middle East, including the importance of keeping the Strait of Hormuz open, U.S. envoy to India Sergio Gor said in a post on X. (Reporting by Shilpa Jamkhandikar; Editing by YP Rajesh)

item.title: Iran toughens negotiating stance amid mediation efforts, sources say
item.description: By Alexander Cornwell and Nazih OsseiranTEL AVIV/BEIRUT, March 24 (Reuters) - Israel will occupy southern Lebanon up to the Litani River to create a "defensive buffer", Defence Minister Israel Katz said on Tuesday, spelling out for the first time Israel's intent to seize territory amounting to nearly a tenth of Lebanon.At a meeting with the military chief of staff, Katz said Israeli forces would "control the remaining bridges and the security zone up to the Litani," a river that meets the Medite

item.title: EU delays April 15 proposal to permanently ban Russian oil imports
item.description: By Kate AbnettBRUSSELS, March 24 (Reuters) - The European Commission will no longer submit a legal proposal to permanently ban Russian oil imports over Moscow's war in Ukraine on April 15 as previously planned, an updated EU legislative agenda showed on Tuesday.An EU official, however, told Reuters the proposal had not been cancelled and would still be published though no longer by the mid-April date due to "current geopolitical developments".

item.title: US-Israeli war on Iran is 'breach of international law': German president
item.description: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier spoke on Tuesday of a "deep rift" with traditional ally the United States and said the US-Israeli war on Iran was a "breach of international law".In unusually strong comments, the German head of state said that just as there was no going back from Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, "there will be no going back to before January 20, 2025", when US President Donald Trump entered the White House for a second time.

item.title: Iran names hardline ex-Revolutionary Guards commander to replace slain security chief
item.description: DUBAI, March 24 (Reuters) - Iran named a former Revolutionary Guards commander and senior figure in the hardline political faction on Tuesday to replace the powerful head of the Supreme National Security Council, Ali Larijani, killed in U.S.-Israeli strikes last week.Mohammad Baqer Zolqadr was appointed as Larijani's successor as secretary of the SNSC, the Iranian president's deputy of communications posted on X on Tuesday.

item.title: Iran oil shock hits global economy as early data signal stagflation risks
item.description: The US-Israeli war with Iran is showing measurable economic impact across the world.

item.title: Iranian ballistic missile intercepted over Lebanon, US Embassy feared as target
item.description: Tensions in Lebanon remain high amid Hezbollah rocket fire toward Israel and intensified Israeli strikes across the country.

item.title: Iran's initial response to US proposal 'not positive', senior Iranian official tells Reuters
item.description: DUBAI, March 25 (Reuters) - Iran's initial response to the U.S. proposal to end the war has not been "positive", a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday, adding that Tehran is still reviewing it.The official said that Tehran's initial response has been delivered to Pakistan to be conveyed to Washington. (Writing by Parisa Hafezi)

item.title: Russia evacuates 163 more staff from Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant, 300 remain
item.description: MOSCOW, March 25 (Reuters) - Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom evacuated a further 163 of its staff from Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant on Wednesday, the state-run RIA news agency reported.It cited Rosatom chief Alexei Likhachev as saying about 300 of the company's staff remained at Bushehr, but more would be leaving.Russia built the existing nuclear plant at Bushehr and Rosatom is constructing additional units there, although it has suspended building work since the United States a

item.title: Cyprus has opened discussion with UK over its bases, president says
item.description: NICOSIA, March 25 (Reuters) - Cyprus has initiated a discussion with London on the future of British bases on the island, its president said on Wednesday, after a drone strike on a military facility this month triggered fears their presence could expose it to the wider Iran conflict.Cypriot politicians and legal experts have long been uneasy with the presence of the two bases on the island, among Britain's most important footholds outside of the United Kingdom and which have supported operations

item.title: Iran rejects Trump's proposal for ceasefire as US dispatches forces
item.description: The news follows a negotiations push by the Trump administration to end the war after more than three weeks of fighting.

item.title: Netanyahu seeks to avoid snap vote as Iran war gives no boost in polls
item.description: By Maayan Lubell and Steven ScheerJERUSALEM, March 25 (Reuters) - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is racing to pass a state budget and stave off early elections he would likely lose, with the war in Iran so far doing little to improve his standing in the polls. item.title: U.N. chief names Arnault as personal envoy for Middle East war
item.description: By David BrunnstromMarch 25 (Reuters) - U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Wednesday named veteran French diplomat Jean Arnault to be his personal envoy on the conflict in the Middle East, saying it was "out of control" and the "world is staring down the barrel of a wider war."Guterres told reporters he had been in close contact with many in the region and around the world and that a number of initiatives for dialogue and peace were underway.
